questions.q: What is a behavioral interview question actually trying to assess?
options: How you behave and work with others under real conditions, not your technical knowledge directly
Whether you memorized the correct SQL syntax
How fast you can write a query on a whiteboard
Whether you can recite the company's mission statement
questions.explain: Behavioral questions predict future behavior from past behavior — ownership, communication, and judgment under pressure — which a technical question or a resume can't show on its own.

questions.q: What do the four letters in STAR stand for?
options: Situation, Task, Action, Result
Story, Topic, Analysis, Response
Setup, Target, Attempt, Review
Scope, Time, Approach, Reflection
questions.explain: STAR structures a behavioral answer as Situation (context), Task (your responsibility), Action (what you did), and Result (what happened).

questions.q: According to this lesson, which STAR beat do candidates skip most often, and why does that hurt the answer?
options: Result — without a stated, concrete outcome, the story doesn't land even if the Action was well told
Situation — interviewers can't follow the story without a long setup
Task — interviewers assume the task from context
Action — most candidates already over-explain this part
questions.explain: Candidates often describe the problem and the fix in detail, then stop without stating the outcome directly. Saying the Result explicitly — a number, a fixed error, a working report — is what makes the story land.

questions.q: Why is this capstone project useful material for behavioral interview stories, according to this lesson?
options: It gave the candidate real moments — a bug to debug, a design decision to defend, a scope change to manage — that map directly onto common behavioral prompts
It removes the need to answer any behavioral questions at all
It's the only acceptable source of interview stories
It guarantees the interviewer will ask about it specifically
questions.explain: A career changer doesn't need years of enterprise history — a small number of specific, well-told stories is enough, and building this capstone already produced real material for at least two or three of them.

questions.q: What is the recommended way to prepare a STAR story before an interview, rather than just thinking it through mentally?
options: Write it out in full STAR form ahead of time and read it aloud to check its length and clarity
Memorize it word for word and recite it exactly the same way every time
Wait until the interview and improvise from memory
Prepare only one story and reuse it for every question asked
questions.explain: A story that's only been thought about tends to wander under pressure. Writing it out once, with a specific Result, and timing it out loud is what makes it deliverable smoothly in the moment.
